***
“안녕, 오빠.”
*You blink, and I’m already grinning at the look on your face.*

“I know you don’t speak Korean,” *I tease, brushing a lock of hair behind my ear, “but that one means hi. And also… something more.” I let that hang for a second—watching your eyes search mine, like you’re trying to remember what it used to mean when I called you that.*

*We’re standing outside a quiet café near Sangsu, tucked behind a wall of ivy and worn brick. I picked it because it felt like a place time might forget us. You’re still taking in the scene—neon signs flickering, couples walking past us with tangled fingers—and I’m already taking in you. The same broad shoulders. The same tired eyes. A little more salt in the hair, maybe. But still you. Still mine, in the ways that count.*

“I can’t believe you actually came,” *I say, pushing the door open.* “I thought you were just flirting when you said you missed me.” *I lead you in, order us something sweet, then find the corner booth—low lighting, soft cushions, enough space for secrets.*

*We sit. My knee brushes yours under the table, and I don’t move it away.*

“So,” I say, tracing a slow circle in the condensation on my glass, “do you remember the first time I saw it?”

*Your eyes shift. I smile like I’ve already undressed the memory.*

“In your car. Backseat. Middle of nowhere. You’d driven us out past the suburbs—no streetlights, just moonlight cutting through the fog on the windshield. I was pretending to be shy, legs tucked under me, but you knew. You always knew.”

*I lift my drink, take a sip, then speak through the steam.*

“You unzipped slowly. Like you were warning me. And then—god.” *I shake my head slightly, laughing under my breath.* “It was the first time I really understood the word ‘white.’ Not your skin. Not your voice. That thing between your legs. Thick, pale, veined like marble. Like it didn’t belong inside me—but it did. Every inch.”

*I glance up through my lashes.*

“You stretched me so wide I saw stars. I remember biting your jacket to keep from screaming. The whole car rocked. I couldn’t walk straight for two days.”

*My voice dips lower now, husky.*

“You said sorry after. I said thank you.”

*A beat.*

“Are you going to make me say it again, 오빠?”
